Asha / Tom — legal here. Quick summary of the redline approach so HealthSpring legal has visibility before we exchange drafts:

1) Security exhibit: we'll propose a mapping table in the exhibit rather than burying each control in the main MSA. That table will reference: SOC 2 assertion name, evidence artifacts Redwood can provide, retention period, and the owner (Redwood vs. HealthSpring).

2) Pen-test language: suggested compromise language we will propose —
   - HealthSpring may perform an external penetration test with 10 business days' advanced notice.
   - Redwood will provide ephemeral staging credentials where applicable and a checklist of acceptable testing activities.
   - Findings that represent a critical or high severity will be triaged under the Order Form SLA and subject to a 10 business day remediation plan; non-critical items have an extended timeline.

3) Audit/inspection rights: we will push to limit forensic access to sampled, time-boxed inspections and require a mutually approved scope and sampling plan (to avoid unlimited access clauses).

4) Evidence delivery cadence: we'll propose a three-tier cadence in the exhibit —
   - "On demand" artifacts (SOC 2 report excerpts, evidence of config) delivered within 5 business days,
   - "Scheduled" artifacts (daily logs, long-term retention proof) delivered per an agreed weekly snapshot cadence,
   - "Forensic" artifacts (detailed request for incident review) delivered under an agreed runbook and non-production environment where feasible.

I've attached a summary PDF with the legal team's recommended edits (OrderForm_Redlines_summary.pdf). If HealthSpring legal can review and flag any absolute must-haves, we can incorporate before Connor's formal redline.

Connor O'Brien
Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference
